entries.name: Soft g-frames in soft Hilbert spaces
entries.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and analyze soft $g$-frames in soft Hilbert spaces, extending generalized frame theory to parameterized uncertainty models. We establish the completeness of the direct sum of soft Hilbert spaces and prove that the associated soft pre-$g$-frame operator $T_Λ$ is well-defined and bounded with unconditionally convergent series representations. Furthermore, we show that the soft $g$-frame operator $S_Λ$ is a bounded, self-adjoint, and strictly positive element of the unital soft Banach algebra $\mathcal{B}(\tilde{\mathcal{U}})$, and we prove its invertibility via the soft Neumann series and derive two-sided operator bounds for its inverse. We characterize the canonical dual soft $g$-frame, establish the unconditional soft $g$-frame decomposition theorem, and construct induced pairs of dual soft frames from dual soft $g$-frames. Finally, an analytical example with parameter-dependent metrics illustrates the matrix representations, verifies the optimality of the frame bounds via Rayleigh quotients, and confirms the reconstruction formula.

entries.name: Hörmander properties of discrete-time Markov processes
entries.abstract: We develop a general framework for establishing smoothing properties of inhomogeneous discrete-time Markov processes under a local weak space-time Hörmander condition imposed at the initial point. Our analysis is carried out directly at the discrete level, combining a Malliavin-inspired differential calculus allowing non-Gaussian increments with covariance non-degeneracy estimates specific to this setting. This yields smooth densities and quantitative derivative bounds for Gaussian-regularized discrete processes, as well as quantitative semigroup regularization and density-derivative bounds for the limiting time-inhomogeneous diffusion. We further establish a quantitative invariance principle in total variation for discrete processes sharing the same infinitesimal drift and covariance. The convergence rate is of order $δ^{\frac{1}{2}}$, improves to order $δ$ under a simple moment cancellation condition, and more generally inherits higher weak approximation rates for smooth test functions.

entries.name: Isometric classification of the $L^{p}$-spaces of infinite dimensional Lebesgue measure
entries.abstract: We investigate the isometric structure of $L^{p}$-spaces for the infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure $(\mathbb{R}^{\mathbb{N}},μ)$. Under the continuum hypothesis (CH) we prove $L^{p}(μ)\cong \ell^{p}(\mathfrak{c},L^{p}[0,1])$, where $\mathfrak{c}$ denotes the cardinality of the continuum, and without CH we obtain an isometric, complemented copy of $\ell^{p}(\mathfrak{c},L^{p}[0,1])$ inside $L^{p}(μ)$. In a general framework, we characterize precisely when $L^{p}(ν)\cong \ell^{p}(κ,L^{p}[0,1])$ and classify all such isometries.

entries.name: Top of the spectrum of discrete Anderson Hamiltonians with correlated Gaussian potentials
entries.abstract: We investigate the top of the spectrum of discrete Anderson Hamiltonians with correlated Gaussian noise in the large volume limit. The class of Gaussian noises under consideration allows for long-range correlations. We show that the largest eigenvalues converge to a Poisson point process and we obtain a very precise description of the associated eigenfunctions near their localisation centres. We also relate these localisation centres with the locations of the maxima of the noise. Actually, our analysis reveals that this relationship depends in a subtle way on the behaviour near $0$ of the covariance function of the noise: in some situations, the largest eigenfunctions are not associated with the largest values of the noise.

entries.name: On models of affine arithmetic
entries.abstract: By affine arithmetic is meant the set of affine consequences of Peano arithmetic. This is a continuous theory which is studied in the framework of affine logic, a sublogic of continuous logic. Affine arithmetic is undecidable. Also, its models are generally lattice ordered and carry a nontrivial metric. Classical models are then characterized as those which are linearly ordered. In this paper, the affine variants of several classical results in Peano arithmetic are proved. In particular, an affine form of Gaifman's splitting theorem is proved.

entries.name: An Anchor-and-Propagate Scheme for Certified $O(n^2)$ Computation of Shapley Vectors in Cooperative Product Games
entries.abstract:
For a general cooperative game, the Shapley values of the players need not be related, but for cooperative product games they are closely linked; identifying and exploiting these relations is one purpose of this study. We consider a network of \(n\) devices that participate independently with probabilities \(p_1,\dots,p_n\), giving the plausibility game \(T(S)=1-\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i)\), whose Shapley values are \(φ_i=p_i\int_0^1\prod_{j
e i}(1-p_jt)\,dt\). Since \(T=1-w\) for the product game \(w(S)=\prod_{i\in S}(1-p_i)\), the results transfer to product games with factors in \([0,1]\). Our main contribution is an \emph{anchor-and-propagate} scheme: once \(φ_1\) is computed exactly, the exact identities \(φ_i=c_iφ_1+p_i(p_i-p_1)B_i\) and \(φ_i=φ_1+(p_i-p_1)J_i\), with \(c_i=p_i/p_1\) and one-dimensional integrals \(B_i\le	frac12J_i\), give the remaining \(n-1\) values in \(O(n)\) total time with certified error bounds. For small \(S_i=\sum_{j
e1,i}p_j\) we use a truncated Bonferroni expansion of \(B_i\); for large \(S_i\), a new estimator with relative error \(O(m_i^2/S_i^2)\), \(m_i=\max_{j
e1,i}p_j\). The anchor is computed by Gauss--Legendre quadrature in \(O(n^2)\) operations or, without irrational nodes, exactly by polynomial expansion. The whole vector costs \(	frac32n^2+O(n)\) operations, about half the exact baseline and less than QuadraSHAP. For \(n=100\), the scheme uses \(1.8	imes10^4\) operations with errors below \(3.4	imes10^{-7}\), within a certified bound of \(2.1	imes10^{-6}\); permutation sampling (Castro et al.) needs \(4	imes10^7\) operations for an error of \(7.9	imes10^{-4}\), controlled only in probability. We also give an anchor-free closed-form approximation with an explicit error bound, and a self-contained derivation of Shapley's formula using combinatorial identities and the Beta function.

entries.name: A multiscale discrete-to-continuum framework for structured population models
entries.abstract: Mathematical models of biological populations commonly use discrete structure classes to capture trait variation among individuals (e.g. age, size, phenotype, intracellular state). Upscaling these discrete models into continuum descriptions can improve analytical tractability and scalability of numerical solutions. Common upscaling approaches based solely on Taylor expansions may, however, introduce ambiguities in truncation order, uniform validity and boundary conditions. To address this, here we introduce a discrete multiscale framework to systematically derive continuum approximations of structured population models. Using the method of multiple scales and matched asymptotic expansions applied to discrete systems, we identify regions of structure space for which a continuum representation is appropriate and derive the corresponding partial differential equations. The leading-order dynamics are given by an advection equation in the bulk domain and advection-diffusion processes in small inner layers about wavefronts. We further derive discrete boundary layer descriptions for regions where the discrete model cannot be approximated by a continuum description. Finally, we demonstrate the method on a simple lipid-structured model for early atherosclerosis and verify consistency between the discrete and continuum descriptions. The multiscale framework we present can be applied to other heterogeneous systems with discrete structure in order to obtain appropriate upscaled dynamics with asymptotically consistent boundary conditions.

entries.name: Induced replication and the assessment of models
entries.abstract: The paper is a first attempt at a foundation of inference for the assessment of semiparametric and other high-dimensional models, seeking reconciliation with the low-dimensional Fisherian foundations by replacing out-of-sample prediction error as a criterion for semiparametric model assessment by a type of within-sample prediction error. We highlight the possibility, in some contexts, of avoiding the usual semiparametric considerations, including estimation of unparametrised nuisance components and the associated difficulties of tuning-parameter choice that blur the distinction between estimation and model assessment. A key aspect of the work is the inducement of replication under the postulated model, the route to which being context-specific but based on structural properties of the model. The ideas are isolated through examples.

entries.name: On Word Representations and Embeddings in Complex Matrices
entries.abstract: Embeddings of word structures into matrix semigroups provide a natural bridge between combinatorics on words and linear algebra. However, low-dimensional matrix semigroups impose strong structural restrictions on possible embeddings. Certain finitely generated groups admit faithful representations in SL(2, C) and other similar matrix groups. On the other hand, it is known that the product of two free semigroups on two generators cannot be embedded into the 2x2 complex matrices. In this paper we study embeddings of word structures into low-dimensional matrix semigroups over the complex numbers and develop new techniques for constructing word representations of the Euclidean Bianchi groups. These representations provide a symbolic framework and a natural first step towards analysing fundamental decision problems in 2x2 matrix semigroups.

entries.name: Complex deformations of the circle: Group cohomology and Virasoro uniformization
entries.abstract: We approach the question of complexification of the diffeomorphism group of the circle by considering real-analytic maps from the circle into the punctured complex plane with winding number +1. Such complex deformations form an infinite-dimensional manifold with partially defined inversion and composition operations, smooth in the sense of Frölicher structures, and with Lie algebra relations at the identity given by the Witt algebra. We compute their second group cohomology with real coefficients. It is generated by two cocycles: One cocycle extending the Bott-Thurston cocycle related to the Gelf'and-Fuks cocycle of the Virasoro algebra, and another Euler class cocycle combining mean rotation and conformal radius. Complex deformations act naturally on the (infinite-dimensional) Segal moduli spaces of Riemann surfaces with enumerated and analytically parametrized boundary components, equipping them with smooth Frölicher structures. We prove a Virasoro uniformization theorem: The tangent spaces of the Segal moduli spaces are spanned by vector fields induced by the Witt algebra. Finally, we relate the actions of complex deformations to Fenchel-Nielsen coordinates and Schiffer variation on finite-dimensional moduli spaces of bordered hyperbolic surfaces with one marked point on each boundary component.

entries.name: A new upwind DG scheme for a Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy model of tumor growth
entries.abstract: In this work, we develop a new numerical scheme for a Cahn-Hilliard-Darcy model that describes tumor growth in a fluid-saturated porous medium. First, we derive a physically consistent model from the general framework proposed in [35] that guarantees mass conservation and pointwise bounds on the phase-field and nutrient variables, with a decreasing energy law. The resulting model couples the evolution of tumor cells via a Cahn-Hilliard equation with a diffusion equation for the nutrients through chemotactic interactions and extends the model in [1] by introducing the effect of a surrounding fluid described by Darcy's law. Subsequently, we propose a fully discrete scheme that combines an upwind discontinuous Galerkin method in space and a convex splitting strategy in time, which inherits the fundamental properties of the continuous model: mass conservation, pointwise bounds and a discrete energy law that mimics the one of the continuous model up to some residual terms. Our theoretical analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments that demonstrate the robustness of the proposed scheme and show the influence of the surrounding fluid on the tumor evolution.

entries.name: General Lagrangian formulations for mixed-antisymmetric tensor fields on flat backgrounds
entries.abstract: We present, for the first time, local Lagrangian formulations for (ir)reducible integer higher-spin massless and massive Poincare group representations subject to Young tableau with $k$ columns $Y[\hat{s}_1,\hat{s}_2,...,\hat{s}_k]$ in $d$-dimensional Minkowski space-time. The particles are described in a metric-like formulation by tensor fields carrying $k$ groups of antisymmetric Lorentz indices $Φ_{μ^1[{\hat{s}_1}],μ^2[{\hat{s}_2}],..., μ^k[{\hat{s}_k}]}$ using the BRST procedure with both the complete operator $Q$ and incomplete $Q_c$ BRST operators. Starting from a description of bosonic mixed-antisymmetric higher-spin fields in terms of an auxiliary Fock space associated with a special Poincare module, we realize a conversion of the initial operator constraint system into a system of first-class operator constraints. For this purpose, we find, for the first time, by means of Verma module the auxiliary representations of the constraint subalgebra, to be isomorphic due to Howe duality to $so(k,k)$ algebra, and containing the subsystem of second-class operators in terms of new oscillator variables forming the Fock module. An unconstrained (with $Q$) and constrained (with $Q_c$ and BRST invariant algebraic constraints) gauge Lagrangian formulations with equivalent dynamics, but different configuration spaces are found. We outline within $Q_c$-approach the concept of consistent local cubic interactions and evaluate the candidate structure of cubic vertices involving $p\geq 3$ copies of interacting massless mixed-antisymmetric fields.

entries.name: Logarithmic Stability for an Inverse Source Problem in a Coupled Nonlinear Helmholtz System
entries.abstract: We consider an inverse source problem for a coupled nonlinear Helmholtz system motivated by second-harmonic generation. For a known susceptibility bounded away from zero, we prove that small real-valued sources are uniquely determined by the full first Fréchet derivative of the nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann map at a fixed small real boundary value. Under an a priori Sobolev bound, we derive a conditional logarithmic stability estimate. The proof uses linearization, complex geometric optics solutions for a matrix Schrödinger equation, and interpolation.

entries.name: Free Boundary Propagation of a Thin-Film Equation with Nonlinear Diffusion: Scale-Consistent Methods for Optimal Results
entries.abstract: We investigate the free boundary propagation of a non-linear degenerate parabolic problem with both fourth and second order non-linearities, which may be used to model viscous thin-film flow in the regime of weak slippage with an additional contributions from a singular disjoining pressure brought forth by inter-molecular forces. By carefully treating the individual scaling behaviors of the non-linearities, we obtain asymptotically optimal upper and lower bounds on the rate of forward support propagation. These rates show that the fourth-order operator dominates the propagation rate on short time scales, but the long-term rate of propagation is controlled by the second-order operator. We estimate further the time at which this trade-off in propagation rate occurs. Lastly, we examine sufficient conditions to ensure that the free boundary does not immediately advance in a given direction, leading to a detailed picture of how the competition between the second/fourth-order operators influence the free boundary dynamics of solutions.

entries.name: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
entries.abstract: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

entries.name: Cellular Algebra of A2 webs
entries.abstract: We introduce a diagram algebra $\mathcal{K}_L$ based on Kuperberg's $A_2$-webs and prove a Schur--Weyl duality $\mathcal{K}_L \cong \operatorname{End}_{U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)}((V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L})$, where $V^\pm$ are the fundamental representations of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$. By self-duality of $V^+\oplus V^-$, $\mathcal{K}_L$ is a natural $A_2$ analogue of the Temperley--Lieb algebra. We construct an explicit cellular structure for $\mathcal{K}_L$, with the web basis as its cellular basis and cell modules indexed by dominant $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$-weights. The bases of these modules are parametrized by dominant lattice paths via a recursive growth algorithm. Using this structure, we determine local generators of $\mathcal{K}_L$ and establish web formulations of the first and second fundamental theorems of invariant theory. In particular, we show that the braid-group image, augmented by local idempotents, does not generate $\mathcal{K}_L$, and identify an additional local generator. Finally, we derive a bimodule decomposition of $(V^+ \oplus V^-)^{\otimes L}$, yielding a complete set of irreducible $\mathcal{K}_L$-modules for formal or generic $q$.

entries.name: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation
entries.abstract: We give an affirmative answer to the abstract group problem for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is universal and finitely universal, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.

entries.name: A remark on the AI proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture
entries.abstract: We give a geometric interpretation of the projection and reconstruction underlying the Open AI's characteristic-two proof of the Deligne--Drinfeld conjecture. Using the double covering and filling a puncture, we construct a morphism on normalized level-two associators with an explicit inverse on its image. We compute the restricted tangent reconstruction in the pro-2 realization and identify the leading coefficient maps with those of the OpenAI proof, making its implicit reconstruction explicit.

entries.name: Sparse Fault Detection in Linear Systems: Equivalence of GLR Tests and $\ell_1$-regularized Least Squares
entries.abstract: This paper studies the detection of an impulsive fault of unknown time and input channel in a linear system with unknown initial state and Gaussian measurement noise. First, we show that the generalized likelihood ratio test, after the initial state is eliminated by projection onto the parity space, is the zero-solution test of a weighted lasso with an unpenalized nuisance block; the regularization parameter is the test threshold, and for unknown noise variance the same holds for the square-root lasso. Second, we show that the null distribution depends on the system only through a Gram matrix, so that the threshold is computed exactly and offline, and we compare it with closed-form bounds. Third, we characterize the fraction of a fault that survives the projection: we give it in closed form through observability Gramians, we show that it converges to a geometrically decaying profile for strictly stable systems, and that, for systems with unit-modulus modes, it grows linearly with the fault time as a fraction of the record length. Numerical studies, including a two-input, two-output example, illustrate the results.

entries.name: The effect of policy cancellation on the risk of an insurance portfolio
entries.abstract: For an insurance portfolio modelled by a large number of i.i.d. losses, the average loss converges to its expected value by the law of large numbers, reflecting the diversification effect of pooling risks. Policy cancellations reduce the portfolio size and thereby weaken this effect. We quantify the resulting increase in risk by applying risk measures to the average loss before and after the cancellation of policies. For a portfolio of size $n$, we show that the impact of cancelling a single contract is of order $n^{-3/2}$, while the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts has an effect of order $n^{-1/2}$. We further extend the proportional cancellation regime to heterogeneous portfolios with different cancellation rates and risk characteristics across segments. These asymptotic results provide a quantitative basis for assessing surrender fees and cancellation costs from the insurer's perspective. We complement the theoretical analysis with numerical results for representative life insurance products, illustrating the magnitude of cancellation costs and the effect of portfolio aggregation. The two regimes require different techniques. For the cancellation of a fixed proportion of contracts, we employ central limit theorems in Wasserstein distance. For the cancellation of a single contract, we combine Kantorovich-Rubinstein duality with higher-order distributional approximations based on the Edgeworth and Cornish-Fisher expansions.

entries.name: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
entries.abstract: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

entries.name: Counting shorter even cycles in graphs forbidding an even cycle
entries.abstract: For graphs $H$ and $F$, the generalized Turán number $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,F)$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Let $C_m$ be a cycle on $m$ vertices. Liu and Wu (2026) proved that, for fixed integers $k>\ell\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})=\left(\frac{(k-1)_\ell}{2\ell}+o(1)\right)n^\ell$, where $(k-1)_\ell=(k-1)\cdots(k-\ell)$. In this paper, we determine the exact value of $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})$ for all sufficiently large $n$ and characterize the unique extremal graph.

entries.name: Mixed-integer programming formulations for the quadratic bin packing problem: linearization, hybridization, and enhancements
entries.abstract: The quadratic bin packing problem (QBPP) extends the classical bin packing problem by incorporating pairwise dissimilarity values between items assigned to the same bin. The objective is to minimize the total cost, composed of the cost associated with the number of bins used and the sum of pairwise dissimilarity values for items assigned to the same bin, subject to the bin-capacity constraints. We study the quadratic programming formulation together with a broad family of equivalent mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) formulations for the QBPP based on classical linearization techniques. We analyze the relationships among the linear programming relaxations of the MILP formulations and strengthen several of these relaxations by exploiting the structure of the QBPP. We further introduce the first hybrid exact formulation for the QBPP that combines elements of two distinct modeling approaches. In particular, we show that the combination of explicit bin patterns and assignment-based representation performs particularly well. For the hybrid formulation, we investigate the effect of item selection, and for both the hybrid and non-hybrid formulations, we study the impact of item ordering on formulation size, relaxation strength and computational performance. Although a recently introduced tailored branch-and-price algorithm remains the state-of-the-art for the QBPP, we show that the proposed ordering-based non-hybrid and hybrid formulations substantially improve computational performance over the best MILP formulation known to the literature, in addition of solving 33 new benchmark instances to optimality.

entries.name: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
entries.abstract: We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio. For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined $(n+1)$-plane. To our knowledge, this is the first such convergence theorem for spherical free boundary MCF in arbitrary codimension. The closed theorem requires additional quadratic pinching for $5\leq n\leq7$, and the free boundary theorem for $4\leq n\leq7$. For $n\geq8$, the necessary quadratic bound follows from quadratic convexity. We also establish preservation of ordinary quadratic pinching $|A|^2\leq c|H|^2$ under spherical free boundary flow for $n\ge2$ and $\frac{9}{8n}\leq c\leq\frac{4}{3n}$, including both endpoints.

entries.name: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
entries.abstract: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function. We perform a thorough analysis in a particular model with two phases, one weakly coupled and one strongly coupled, both corresponding to Calabi-Yau threefolds. General methods are developed in this study and are applied to other models successfully. The integrals for a set of special Chan-Paton representations exhibit critical behaviour around each singular point on the phase boundary. From each of these points emanate ``no entry zones'' where a convergent contour is lost or is forced to traverse Gamma function poles. Knowledge of the special representations and no entry zones is strong enough to uniquely determine the grade restriction rule. In the course of this study, we encounter a problem in Weyl invariance of convergent contours, which forces us to modify the grade restriction criterion. The special representations play an important rôle in the monodromy around the singular point. We also obtain exact results on boundary conditions in supersymmetric QCDs and apply them to understand the low energy behaviour of D-branes in the strong coupling phase.

entries.name: One more curious property of $1729$: The only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with prime $p$
entries.abstract: Florian Luca recently proved that if $2^np^3+1$ is a Carmichael number for some prime $p$ and integer $n\ge1$, then $p=3$. Here we complete the cubic classification by proving that $1729$, Hardy--Ramanujan taxicab number, is the only Carmichael number of the form $2^np^3+1$ with $p$ prime and $n\ge1$. The proof identifies the unique possible multiplicatively dependent prime factor, sharpens the known bound on Fermat prime factors of $2^nk+1$ from $k^2$ to $2k$, derives the explicit bound $n\le2742$, and concludes with a short sieve requiring neither factorisation nor primality testing.

entries.name: Asymptotic analysis of a $3\times3$-doubly periodic random lozenge tiling model of a hexagon
entries.abstract: We study a random lozenge tiling model of a regular hexagon with weights that are doubly periodic with period $3$. This model features a smooth phase with six cusp points. We obtain explicit descriptions of the limit shape and the local scaling limits of the correlation kernel. Both limits are expressed as contour integrals on the Harnack curve that underlies the model, or on its double cover that is obtained by gluing together two copies along the support of an equilibrium measure in an external field. Our asymptotic analysis is based on the double contour integral representation of the correlation kernel due to Duits and Kuijlaars. This double contour integral contains a factor that is given in terms of the solution of a Riemann-Hilbert problem for matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials. The asymptotic behavior of this Riemann-Hilbert problem was recently studied by one of the authors using the Deift-Zhou method of steepest descent. In this work, we complement this approach with the asymptotic analysis of the double contour integral. The integrals are moved to the double cover of the Harnack curve. We analyze the effect of the first two transformations of the Deift-Zhou method, and deform the contours to the relevant saddle points. We visualize our asymptotic analysis on the amoeba of the Harnack curve, in the spirit of the work of Berggren and Borodin on the doubly periodic Aztec diamond.

entries.name: A complete classification of isometries of quasihyperbolic domains
entries.abstract: We classify all surjective quasihyperbolic isometries between arbitrary proper planar domains. Apart from Euclidean similarities, the orientation-preserving isometries are reciprocal maps on sectors or punctured planes and explicit complex-power maps on logarithmic spiral sectors. In particular, orientation-preserving planar quasihyperbolic isometries need not be Möbius. As consequences, we obtain similarity rigidity when either domain has finite inradius, for multiply connected domains other than punctured planes, and for $C^1$ domains other than half-planes. The $C^1$ conclusion strengthens Hästö's corresponding result for planar $C^3$ domains. Our planar classification, together with Richard's classification in dimensions $n\geq3$, completely solves the quasihyperbolic isometry problem between proper subdomains of $\mathbb R^n$ in every dimension $n\geq2$. As an application, we extend to dimension two the characterization of pointed Gromov--Hausdorff convergence of quasihyperbolic domains obtained by Herron, Richard, and Snipes.

entries.name: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
entries.abstract: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\neΛ\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(Λ)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $Λ\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii. As part of the proof, we generalize Meyer's notion of lighthouse measures to higher codimension and introduce lighthouse manifolds, which we characterize, up to a monomial change of coordinates, as the torus parts of Lee--Yang varieties.

entries.name: Parameter estimation for discretely observed rough fractional interacting particle systems
entries.abstract: We study parametric inference for interacting particle systems driven by independent fractional Brownian motions, based on discrete observations of all particles over a fixed time horizon. Our goal is to estimate an unknown drift parameter in the joint limit as the number of particles increases and the observation mesh vanishes. For $H>\frac 12$, we construct contrast based estimators by extending the discrete time least squares approach of Neuenkirch and Tindel to the interacting setting. For the rough regime $H\in(\frac 14,\frac 12)$, we introduce a modified contrast and use the stochastic sewing lemma to handle the first order approximations available from discrete observations. Our analysis combines the propagation of chaos for the associated fractional McKean Vlasov equation with estimates controlling the temporal discretization error. When the Hurst parameter and the diffusion coefficient are known, we establish strong consistency and asymptotic normality of the proposed estimators. The asymptotic results reveal an interplay between the number of particles and the temporal discretization: the convergence rate with respect to the observation mesh changes at $H=\frac 34$, while the asymptotic normality holds in both regimes considered. We further develop a joint estimation procedure for the drift parameter, the Hurst parameter, and the diffusion coefficient, extending quadratic-variation methods for fractional Brownian motion to the interacting particle framework. Numerical experiments illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators.

entries.name: Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops
entries.abstract: We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.

entries.name: A Well-Separated Pair Decomposition of Linear Size for Unit-Disk Graphs
entries.abstract: We prove that every connected Euclidean-weighted unit-disk graph on $n$ vertices has a $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition of size $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. This resolves an open problem posed by Gao and Zhang in 2003. We also show that this bound is tight: there are connected unit-disk graphs for which any $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition has size $Ω(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log (1/\varepsilon))$.

entries.name: Two results on rich-neighbour $5$-colouring of subcubic graphs
entries.abstract: A rich-neighbour edge-colouring is a proper edge-colouring in which every non-isolated edge has an adjacent edge whose neighbours have pairwise distinct colours. Petruševski and Škrekovski conjectured that every connected subcubic loopless multigraph distinct from $K_4$ admits such a colouring with five colours. We prove the conjecture for two classes: claw-free subcubic loopless multigraphs and $2$-connected subcubic outerplanar loopless multigraphs. The bound is sharp in both classes, as witnessed by the diamond $K_4-e$.

entries.name: Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition
entries.abstract: We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S. We identify the Poisson and Furstenberg boundaries of these groups. This applies in particular to reductive algebraic groups over local fields.

entries.name: The n-th Zbáganu constant
entries.abstract: In this paper, we introduce the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Banach spaces and investigate its basic properties. We establish some inequalities which give the relationship between the $n$-th Zbáganu constant and two other constants, namely the $n$-th Von Neumann-Jordan constant and the $n$-th James constant. In addition, we determine the values of the $n$-th Zbáganu constant for Lebesgue spaces, Morrey spaces, and discrete Morrey spaces.

entries.name: Diffusion-Score-Based Joint Topology Identification and Generative Particle Filtering
entries.abstract: Inferring the interaction graph of a networked system while tracking its latent state is central to infrastructure, environmental, and brain networks. Joint identification of interaction topology and latent network states is challenging when observations are intermittent and transition noise is unknown and non-Gaussian. We develop TopoScore-FAF, a diffusion-score-based framework for joint topology identification and generative particle filtering. The graph governs a leaky-diffusion conditional mean, while a frozen diffusion emulator represents the centered transition residual, avoiding the structural ambiguity of unrestricted generative models. First, we establish a score--topology duality that expresses edge-wise transition likelihood gradients as projections of the residual diffusion score. This enables topology learning without evaluating transition densities or differentiating through the generative sampler. Second, we develop diffusion-score-based topology identification with guarantees of identifiability under intermittent observations and invariance of the population minimizer across diffusion noise levels. Sufficient smoothing yields global strong convexity for bounded-plus-Gaussian residuals. As smoothing vanishes, the asymptotic covariance of the state-pair estimator decreases toward the Cramér--Rao bound, with a strict advantage over Gaussian quasi-likelihood under an edge-relevant non-Gaussianity condition. Third, we construct a topology-conditioned generative particle filter that combines guided residual sampling with score-driven graph updates. We establish mean-square closed-loop error bounds under a step-size-independent small-gain condition. The resulting framework uses the graph to structure state propagation and the estimated states to refine the graph. Synthetic and real-data experiments demonstrate its benefits under non-Gaussian forcing.

entries.name: Finding four vertices of a square of area $n$ in a grid by geometric construction
entries.abstract: In this study, we consider geometric construction in an infinite square grid. Our purpose is to find efficient methods for constructing a square of area $n\in\mathbb{N}$ based on arithmetic properties of the sum of squares. As a consequence, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we derive the optimal number of construction steps required to determine the four vertices of the square. Furthermore, we classify all positive integers into three classes according to these optimal numbers.

entries.name: Homeomorphic Sobolev Extensions to Jordan Domains and the inner distance
entries.abstract: Given a Jordan domain $Ω$, we characterize the situation where a given parametrization (or all parametrizations) $\varphi:\partial\mathbb D\to\partialΩ$ has (have) a homeomorphic $W^{1,1}$-extension $f_{\varphi}:\overline{\mathbb D}\to\overlineΩ$.

entries.name: The shape function of last passage percolation up to constants
entries.abstract: We determine the diagonal shape function of lattice last passage percolation up to dimension-dependent constants and characterize its finiteness by a tail integral. The proof transfers estimates from an entropy-controlled Poisson model whose quadratic penalty makes the curvature dependence explicit. For critical tails of exponent $q$ in dimension $q\geq 2$, the mean passage time has order $n(\log n)^{(q+1)/(2q)}$, proving sharpness of the logarithmic exponent in the lower bound of Ganguly, Ginsburg and Nam.

entries.name: Power projections, Gram structures, and finite-field lifting of Butson Hadamard matrices
entries.abstract: In this paper we investigate the algebraic properties of Hadamard powers of Butson Hadamard matrices $H\in \mathrm{BH}(n,3p)$, and show that for certain parameter values the cube root projection matrix $H^{\circ p}$ has the same structure as the adjacency matrix of a strongly regular graph. Then, by using a simple eigenvalue analysis we show, among other results, the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(17,15)$ matrices. For other parameter values, a more in-depth study and in particular, a complete classification of all possible projection matrices is necessary. We carry out this task for the case of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices, and using finite field techniques we show that none of these projections can be lifted up to form a Butson matrix. In particular, we show the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(16,15)$ matrices for the first time.

entries.name: Structure-Preserving Neural Approximation of Convex, Semiconvex, and Quasiconvex Functions
entries.abstract: Input convex neural networks provide a natural way to enforce convexity globally through architectural constraints. We study how this structure-preserving approximation framework extends to semiconvex, quasiconvex, and convex transformable functions. For $C^{1,1}$ convex functions on compact convex domains, we establish the sharp $W^{1,p}$ minimax rate $m^{-1/d}$ under max-affine approximation with $m$ affine pieces, and show that every max-affine function admits an exact bounded-width ICNN representation with complexity linear in $m$. The same $W^{1,p}$ approximation rate extends to semiconvex functions through quadratic lifting and to convex transformable functions through monotone composition. For general Lipschitz quasiconvex functions, we develop a quantitative finite-probe approximation theory based on monotone responses to affine projections and obtain a structure-preserving IqCNN with an $L^\infty$ approximation guarantee. We further show that these approximation results extend to ReLU-transferable smooth activations, including Softplus and ELU. Numerical experiments on PDE-based approximation problems compare the proposed architectures with parameter-matched MLPs and validation-tuned shape penalties, demonstrating global structural validity without penalty tuning while maintaining competitive approximation accuracy. Overall, the results identify recoverable convex latent structure as the key mechanism enabling gradient-level structure-preserving approximation beyond convexity.

entries.name: Global stability and nonlinear asymptotics for the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity
entries.abstract: We study the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity, a positive coefficient $λ+μ>0$ in the divergence term, and full heat conduction. Horizontal viscosity does not dissipate vertical shear derivatives, while thermal diffusion is coupled to the compressible variables. For small $H^2$ perturbations of a constant equilibrium, we construct global strong solutions. Additional spatial localization yields anisotropic decay through second order, convergence of the full $H^2$ norm, and horizontal Gaussian profiles determined by an effective velocity datum. The third-order behavior contains nonlinear contributions: horizontal viscous heating generates a differentiated Newton potential in temperature, while compressible transport slows the decay of the potential velocity. We prove the corresponding bounds with exponents $17/8$ and $2$; for each exponent, we construct a fixed datum in the corresponding class for which every larger exponent fails. For each fixed initial datum, however, the corresponding time-weighted norms tend to zero as $t\to\infty$. Smallness of the first vertical derivative of the initial velocity in the horizontal mixed norm improves the vertical decay estimates and restores the linear third-order temperature rate. Both the existence and decay results require only $H^2$ Sobolev regularity of the initial data.

entries.name: A Batched Discrepancy Principle for Stochastic Landweber-Kaczmarz Iteration and its Application to EIT
entries.abstract: We consider an inverse problem given as ill-posed system of possibly nonlinear operator equations between Hilbert spaces. To solve the problem we use a stochastic mini-batch Landweber-Kaczmarz method, drawing uniformly a subset of equations in each step. As an a posteriori stopping rule, we introduce a batched version of the discrepancy principle, in which only the residual of the selected batches is monitored. Under the tangential cone condition, we establish the convergence of the iterates for exact data, the convergence of the regularized iterates for noisy data under an a priori choice of the stopping index, and the convergence of the method when it is terminated by the proposed batched discrepancy principle. Numerical experiments for the electrical impedance tomography problem illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the performance of the method for different batch sizes.

entries.name: Critical Gaussian Asymptotics for Directional Superoscillations: STFT and Gabor Consequences
entries.abstract: We study directional Aharonov--Berry superoscillations in $\R^d$ with widening anisotropic Gaussian envelopes. We prove that the rescaled total $L^2$ mass has a sharp transition governed by the matrix $D=Q-(a^2-1)vv^T$. At criticality, $D$ has a one-dimensional kernel, and the mass obeys an exact $N^{d/2+1/4}$ law with an explicit Gamma-function constant. After anisotropic rescaling, the intensity converges globally in $L^1$ to a transverse Gaussian times a longitudinal quartic exponential. Moyal's identity gives the corresponding total STFT-energy law, but does not imply a local phase-space concentration theorem. We compare these global statements with the earlier quartic critical-window analysis of Berry and Shukla for periodic superoscillations. Supporting results include quantitative fixed-Gaussian STFT expansions, entire-growth convergence with a critical-step obstruction, and conditional Gabor-frame and dual-window expansions. Weighted STFT estimates for polynomial electric-field evolution are obtained as applications. No claim of priority is made for quartic criticality, qualitative STFT supershift preservation, or polynomial electric-field persistence as such.

entries.name: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
entries.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=λ(1+t)^{-μ}$ with $0<μ<1$, $λ>0$, or $μ=1$, $λ>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the spatially dependent damping coefficient, even though its contribution persists for all time. We also obtain decay estimates of order $\varepsilon(1+t)^{-μ}$ for the derivatives $u_t$, $v_t$, and $v_x$, together with a pointwise estimate for $u_x$ involving the spatial coefficient $a(x)$. The main ingredient is a time-uniform $L^\infty$ estimate for an inhomogeneous coupled transport system with a non-small spatial coefficient. Combined with suitable transformations of the Riemann-invariant derivatives, this estimate allows us to control the nonlinear terms and establish global $C^1$ bounds.

entries.name: On the Critical Exponent for a Time--Space Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equation with a Slowly Varying Time-Dependent Source
entries.abstract: We study the Fujita critical exponent for the Cauchy problem $\partial_t^αu+(-Δ)^{θ/2}u=h(t)u^p$ in $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N$, $u(0)=u_0\ge0$, where $α\in(0,1]$, $θ\in(0,2]$, $p>1$, $\partial_t^α$ is the Caputo derivative, and $h(t)\sim t^γ\ell(t)$ for large $t$, with $γ\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\ell$ slowly varying at infinity in the sense of Karamata. For $α=1$ and every $θ\in(0,2]$ we obtain a complete classification. If $γ\le-1$, small data give global solutions for every $p>1$, so there is no Fujita threshold. If $γ>-1$, the critical exponent is $p_c(γ)=1+θ(γ+1)/N$: every nontrivial solution blows up for $1<p<p_c(γ)$, while small global solutions exist for $p>p_c(γ)$. At $p=p_c(γ)$ the slowly varying factor decides: blow-up occurs if $\int_1^\infty t^{-1}\ell(t)dt=\infty$, and small global solutions exist if this integral converges. Hence global existence may occur at the critical exponent, unlike the autonomous case. For $α\in(0,1)$, the memory of the Caputo derivative replaces $γ+1$ by $γ+α$. We prove small-data global existence for every $p>1$ when $γ\le-α$. When $γ>-α$, all nontrivial solutions blow up for $1<p<p_c(γ,α):=1+θ(γ+α)/(Nα)$. If $N<θ$, we also obtain global existence for $p>p_c(γ,α)$, so the classification is complete, and at $p=p_c(γ,α)$ the dichotomy is governed by the boundedness of $\ell$. If $N\geθ$, we obtain global existence for $p>1+(γ+α)/α$, which coincides with $p_c(γ,α)$ when $N=θ$. Finally, a second, purely local blow-up mechanism shows that for $N>θ$ and $γ>αθ/(N-θ)$, $p_c(γ,α)$ is not the Fujita exponent. Our results extend the theorems of Meier (1990) to the nonlocal setting.

entries.name: Sharp integral condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals
entries.abstract: We show that the necessary and sufficient condition for linear growth of greedy lattice animals with nonnegative i.i.d. vertex weights in every dimension $q\ge2$ is the same criterion for linear growth of directed last-passage times. We also obtain two-sided finite-size estimates, up to dimension-dependent constants, for the mean maximal weights of directed paths, lattice animals, valid for every nonnegative weights. These estimates determine the order of mean growth even when growth is superlinear. Since every up-right path from the origin is a lattice animal, the lower bound follows from the corresponding last-passage bound. For the upper bound, we couple the lattice weights to a Poisson process and represent each animal by a polygonal route of length proportional to its size.

entries.name: Intersections of Odd Polygons Revisited
entries.abstract: It is shown that the maximum number of intersection points between the boundaries of a simple $m$-gon and a simple $n$-gon is $mn-(m+n)+3$ for any odd integers $m,n \ge 3$. The previous best upper bound was $mn-(m+n)+C$, for some huge constant $C$.

entries.name: Complete monotonicity of Laplace transform ratios: Density criteria for self-decomposability and additive decomposition
entries.abstract: We prove a complete monotonicity (CM) theorem for ratios of Laplace transforms: if the denominator function is logarithmically convex and the quotient of the two functions is monotone, then the corresponding quotient of Laplace transforms (or, in the opposite monotonicity case, its derivative) is CM. As probabilistic consequences, we obtain density-level criteria for self-decomposability (SD) and additive decomposition (AD) of positive distributions, together with a short proof of the classical Steutel theorem concerning infinite divisibility (ID). These criteria reduce problems typically tackled via special function quotients or Lévy measures to elementary checks on the underlying densities. The main application is to the beta prime distribution and Tricomi's confluent hypergeometric function. In the log-convex range $a\le1$, we prove new cross-parameter additive decompositions and self-convolution additive factorizations for beta prime laws. Equivalently, we establish the complete monotonicity of several quotients of Tricomi functions, providing partial affirmative solutions to a problem of Ismail and Kelker (SIAM J. Math. Anal., 1979) and to two conjectures of Ferreira and Simon (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc., 2023). We also obtain additive factorizations for generalized inverse Gaussian (GIG) laws, expressed as complete monotonicity of ratios of modified Bessel functions. Further examples, including Whittaker-type and logarithmic beta families, illustrate the scope and limitations of the method.

entries.name: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
entries.abstract: We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin. Our approach is based on the so-called signature formula for the Euler characteristic of real algebraic varieties. Moreover, we show that the same approach yields similar results for certain generalizations of the original Sklyanin algebras known as Jacobian Poisson structures. Keywords: Poisson structure, Sklyanin algebra, Casimir function, Casimir foliation, Nambu bracket, Jacobian Poisson structure, Euler characteristic, algebraic formula for the Euler characteristic, bifurcation diagram, isolated singularity of complete intersection, Milnor number

entries.name: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
entries.abstract: Residual-based methods, including physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), physics-informed Kolmogorov--Arnold networks, and some physics-informed neural operator architectures, approximate PDE solutions by minimizing a discrete least-squares loss formed from the PDE and boundary residuals over a prescribed trial class. This structure is shared by classical least-squares Kansa collocation, whose kernel trial spaces admit an established convergence theory. For neural trial classes, approximation power alone does not ensure that discrete residuals control the continuous solution error. For linear elliptic Dirichlet problems, we extend the kernel-based collocation framework to neural trial classes through elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency. Elliptic regularity supplies the PDE estimate relating solution error to continuous residuals. Discrete stability identifies admissible trial subclasses in which continuous residuals are controlled by a computable discrete loss. This step also quantifies the required number of collocation points. Furthermore, the stability analysis naturally demands a scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weight. For the constrained problem, consistency requires accurate comparison functions within the same admissible subclass, a requirement not supplied by neural approximation estimates alone. Specializing to multilayer perceptrons with tanh activations (tanh-MLPs), we construct admissible comparison networks and establish convergence for the constrained residual minimization problem. We further obtain conditional convergence of unconstrained physics-balanced PINNs based on tanh-MLPs under joint network and sampling refinement.

entries.name: Sharp Sobolev thresholds and rapid rotation for Navier--Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation
entries.abstract: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with fractional horizontal dissipation $νΛ_h^{2α}$, $0<α\le1$, and a Coriolis force. There is no vertical dissipation. The scaling-critical Sobolev index is $s_c=5/2-2α$. For $0<α<1$, we prove local Hadamard well-posedness in $H^s$ for $s\ge s_c$; for $α=1$, the range is $s>1/2$. At every prescribed finite rotation rate, norm inflation holds in all remaining positive-order Sobolev spaces for classical solutions with smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, starting from arbitrarily small $H^s$ data in arbitrarily short time. Thus $H^{s_c}$ is a well-posedness space for $0<α<1$, whereas $H^{1/2}$ exhibits norm inflation for $α=1$. These results give sharp Sobolev thresholds for each finite rotation rate. Throughout the well-posedness range, small data yield global solutions with a rotation-independent smallness threshold, and every fixed datum yields a global solution for sufficiently rapid rotation. The nonlinear solution converges to the linear Stokes--Coriolis evolution uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ and in the global dissipation norm as $|Ω|\to\infty$. For spectrally localized data separated from the vertical frequency axis, the convergence rate is $O(|Ω|^{-γ})$ for every $0<γ<1/2$. For $0<α<1$, the energy estimates close at $s=s_c$ without loss of derivatives in isotropic Sobolev spaces, using Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Sobolev trace inequalities, and localized horizontal product estimates. Below $s_c$, norm inflation follows from an approximation by a fixed smooth Euler solution after rescaling. At $(α,s)=(1,1/2)$, viscosity remains fixed under critical rescaling; the construction instead uses a localized scalar shear and conormal analytic stability estimates uniform in the vertical concentration parameters.

entries.name: Isometrically greedy renormings of bidemocratic unconditional bases of Banach spaces
entries.abstract: We show that if a greedy basis of a Banach space has the additional property that its dual basis is also greedy, then the space admits an equivalent norm under which the basis is isometrically greedy. This solves in the positive a question posed by Dilworth, Kutzarova, Odell, Schlumprecht and Zsák in 2014. As an application, we resolve a long-standing problem explicitly posed by Albiac, Ansorena and Wallis in 2017 by proving that any subsymmetric basis of a Banach space is isometrically greedy under a suitable renorming of the ambient space.

entries.name: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
entries.abstract: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

entries.name: Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
entries.abstract: Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_α(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $ν(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $α\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_α(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.

entries.name: Energy decay and asymptotic profile for a system of damped wave equations
entries.abstract: We consider a system of two wave or Klein-Gordon equations on the Euclidean space. One is damped, while the second is only indirectly damped via a coupling term. We are interested in the large time behavior of the solutions. More precisely, we prove energy decay for both components and, when possible, we give their asymptotic profiles. Our proofs are based on spectral analysis. We will see that in our setting the contribution of high frequencies always decays exponentially, so the results depend on the contribution of low frequencies. We observe a diffusive phenomenon as for a single wave equation, but the coupling between the two components gives completely different behaviors, depending on the nature of the equations and the strengths of the damping and coupling.

entries.name: Rademacher and Enflo types in Banach spaces: sharp comparison and orthogonality
entries.abstract: For every \(1<p\le2\), we prove that the optimal universal factor relating the Enflo type \(p\) constant to the Rademacher type \(p\) constant is \(p\), already among finite-dimensional real or complex Banach spaces. Ivanisvili, van Handel, and Volberg [Ann.\ of Math.\ (2) \textbf{192} (2020), 665--678] proved the equivalence with factor \(π/\sqrt{2}\). Areshidze [arXiv:2609.32666v1 (2026)] improved the upper bound to \(p\). Our matching lower bound settles the optimality question posed in that preprint. We also obtain two results for a real Banach space \(X\). \begin{list}{}{\setlength{\leftmargin}{\dimexpr24pt+1.8em\relax}\setlength{\rightmargin}{24pt}\setlength{\labelwidth}{1.4em}\setlength{\labelsep}{0.4em}\setlength{\topsep}{2pt}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}} \item[(a)] For \(1<p<2\), \(X\) has Enflo type \(p\) if and only if the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality holds uniformly over ordered families \((v_i)\) satisfying \[ v_i\perp_B v_j \qquad \text{for all } i<j, \] where \(\perp_B\) denotes Birkhoff--James orthogonality (that is, \(\|v_i+t v_j\|\ge\|v_i\|\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\)). \item[(b)] For \(1<p\le2\), uniform validity of the Rademacher type \(p\) inequality on pairwise isosceles orthogonal families implies that \(X\) has Enflo type \(2p/(p+1)\). \end{list} These results show how Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality reduce the linear estimates needed to establish a metric type property of the whole space.

entries.name: $k-$Absorbing factorization in multiplicative lattices
entries.abstract: We study the multiplicative $C-$lattices generated by principal elements in which every proper element is a finite product of $k-$absorbing elements. We prove that such lattices have Krull dimension at most one. In the modular case, a finite direct product decomposition theorem is obtained.

entries.name: Phase factors and optimal seminorms for polynomial averages of commuting transformations
entries.abstract: For invertible commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1, \ldots, T_\ell$ on a standard probability space, we study polynomial averages along both integers and primes. We provide a rank-based criterion ensuring that, even when the polynomials are linearly dependent, finite-order phase factors are characteristic factors. For polynomials with integer coefficients and zero constant terms, it suffices that the dimension of the space spanned (over $\mathbb{Q}$) by any nonempty subfamily of $k$ polynomials exceeds $k/2$. These phase factors are generated by polynomial phases associated with positive integer powers of the individual transformations and may be strictly smaller than the corresponding Host-Kra factors of the same order. The required order depends only on the number of polynomials and their maximum degree. A four-term example involving a totally ergodic Heisenberg nilsystem shows that this criterion may fail if the equality $k/2$ is permitted. For a family of three polynomials, this criterion is equivalent to the condition that the polynomials are pairwise linearly independent. Consequently, it applies to the family $t, t^2, t^2+t$, where the third polynomial is the sum of the first two. For this specific family, we prove that the optimal orders for the phase factors and the Host-Kra factors are $4, 2, 2$, respectively--a result that holds for both integers and primes. The corresponding optimal seminorms are $U^5(T_1)$, $U^3(T_2)$, and $U^3(T_3)$, which provides an answer to a question posed by Kuca.

entries.name: Mesh Sensitivity of Different Boundary Treatments in High-Order Compact Gas-Kinetic Scheme for Hypersonic Heat-Flux Prediction
entries.abstract: Accurate wall-heat-flux prediction in hypersonic flow depends on both the wall treatment and the available near-wall resolution. This work compares three complete implementations of a gas-kinetic scheme (GKS) for Mach~8.03 laminar flow over an isothermal circular cylinder: a linear Green--Gauss scheme (GG), a compact ghost-cell scheme (GC), and a pointwise one-sided compact scheme (POS). In POS, the stationary isothermal-wall conditions are imposed at the two Gaussian points used by the kinetic wall-flux quadrature. A reference mesh and six meshes in the uniform reduction (UR), log-layer unpacked (LLU), and log-layer packed (LLP) families are used to assess heat-flux sensitivity. At 24 digitized experimental angles, GG has the lowest root-mean-square difference on the reference, UR, and LLP families, whereas POS is closest on the two LLU meshes; GC is not the lowest-RMS scheme on any tested mesh. Hence no treatment is uniformly superior. On the present high-aspect-ratio cylinder grids, GG is the more robust choice except under LLU node redistribution, for which POS is preferable. Uniform reduction produces the largest heat-flux response for all three implementations. The comparison concerns complete schemes and does not isolate the pointwise constraints from differences in reconstruction and geometry representation.

entries.name: Uniqueness of ground state solutions for fractional Schrödinger equations with general nonlinearities
entries.abstract: In 2013, R.L. Frank and E. Lenzmann [R.L. Frank, E. Lenzmann, Uniqueness of non-linear ground states for fractional Laplacians in $\mathbb{R}$, Acta Math. 210 (2) (2013) 261-318] studied the following problem: \begin{align*} (-Δ)^su + u = u^{p-1} \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N, \end{align*} where $s \in (0,1)$, $N = 1$, $p \in (2,2_s^*)$, and $2_s^*$ is the critical fractional Sobolev exponent. They proved that the ground state is unique (up to translations). Then in 2016, they, together with L. Silvestre [R.L. Frank, E. Lenzmann, L. Silvestre, Uniqueness of radial solutions for the fractional Laplacian, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 69 (9) (2016) 1671-1726], showed similar uniqueness results for high dimensions ($N \geq 2$), in which they proposed a challenging open problem to extend their results about non-degeneracy and uniqueness of ground states to nonlinearities $f(u)$ beyond the pure-power case. In this paper, we aim to give an affirmative answer to this open issue for two classes of more general nonlinearities, including the case of sums of powers with certain conditions on exponents.

entries.name: Holomorphic Floer theory I: exponential integrals in finite and infinite dimensions
entries.abstract: In the first of the series of papers devoted to our project ``Holomorphic Floer Theory" we discuss exponential integrals and related wall-crossing structures. We emphasize two points of view on the subject: the one based on the ideas of deformation quantization and the one based on the ideas of Floer theory. Their equivalence is a corollary of our generalized Riemann-Hilbert correspondence. In the case of exponential integrals this amounts to several comparison isomorphisms between local and global versions of de Rham and Betti cohomology. We develop the corresponding theories in particular generalizing Morse-Novikov theory to the holomorphic case. We prove that arising wall-crossing structures are analytic. As a corollary, perturbative expansions of exponential integrals are resurgent. Based on a careful study of finite-dimensional exponential integrals we propose a conjectural approach to infinite-dimensional exponential integrals. We illustrate this approach in the case of Feynman path integral with holomorphic Lagrangian boundary conditions as well as in the case of the complexified Chern-Simons theory. We discuss the arising perverse sheaf of infinite rank as well as analyticity of the corresponding ``Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure". We develop a general theory of quantum wave functions and show that in the case of Chern-Simons theory it gives an alternative description of the Chern-Simons wall-crossing structure based on the notion of generalized Nahm sum. We propose several conjectures about analyticity and resurgence of the corresponding perturbative series.

entries.name: On non-isomorphic universal sofic groups
entries.abstract: We show that there are $2^{\aleph_0}$ non-isomorphic universal sofic groups. This proves a conjecture of Simon Thomas.

entries.name: Limiting partition function for the Mallows model: a conjecture and partial evidence
entries.abstract: Let $S_n$ denote the set of permutations of $n$ labels. We consider a class of Gibbs probability models on $S_n$ that is a subfamily of the so-called Mallows model of random permutations. The Gibbs energy is given by a class of right invariant divergences on $S_n$ that includes common choices such as the Spearman foot rule and the Spearman rank correlation. Mukherjee in 2016 computed the limit of the (scaled) log partition function (i.e. normalizing factor) of such models as $n\rightarrow \infty$. Our objective is to compute the exact limit, as $n\rightarrow \infty$, without the log. We conjecture that this limit is given by the Fredholm determinant of an integral operator related to the so-called Schrödinger bridge probability distributions from optimal transport theory. We provide partial evidence for this conjecture, although the argument lacks a final error bound that is needed for it to become a complete proof.

entries.name: Asymptotic statistics for finite continued fractions with restricted digits
entries.abstract: Zaremba's conjecture concerns a formation of continued fraction expansions for rational numbers with partial quotient bounded by an absolute constant. We present asymptotic estimates for the size of $ε$-thickening of certain fractal sets of bounded-type, which in turn provide a remark on Zaremba's conjecture in an averaging sense. We also discuss a generalisation for complex continued fractions over imaginary quadratic fields.

entries.name: Strong Approximation for the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere
entries.abstract: We study the orbits of solutions to the Markoff-type equation $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + AX + BY + CZ + D$$ in $\mathbb{F}_p$ for fixed integers $A,B,C,D$ under the group $Γ$ generated by \[\begin{split}&V_1: (x, y, z)\mapsto (A + yz - x, y, z),\\ &V_2: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, B + xz - y, z),\text{ and}\\ &V_3: (x, y, z)\mapsto (x, y, C + xy - z).\end{split}\] This equation defines the Relative Character Variety of the Four-Times Punctured Sphere, with $Γ$ arising from the Pure Mapping Class Group. Outside an explicit degeneracy locus, $Γ$ acts transitively on almost all solutions for a density-one set of primes independent of the parameters; the others split into small orbits reflecting finite orbits over $\mathbb{C}$. For ``degenerate'' parameters, we show there are two large orbits (most cases) or four (the rest, excluding $(0, 0, 0, 4)$) for the same primes. These results strengthen for two subfamilies. The first, $$X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 = XYZ + k,\,\,\,k\neq 4,$$ arises in the combinatorial group theory of $\text{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)$. Combined with Chen's work, $Γ$ acts transitively for all large primes, uniformly in $k$, so the $Q$-classification conjecture of McCullough and Wanderley holds over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for $p$ large. By Martin's work, so do their Classification and $T$-Classification Conjectures. The second, $$x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 + a_1x_2x_3 + a_2x_1x_3 + a_3x_1x_2 = (3+a_1+a_2+a_3)x_1x_2x_3,$$ arises from generalized cluster algebras. Our degeneracy notion specializes to that of de Courcy-Ireland, Litman, and Mizuno, whose results similarly imply our orbit count (1, 2, or 4) for all large primes for all nondegenerate and some degenerate surfaces in that family.ds for all sufficiently large primes.

entries.name: Arithmetic limiting laws over shifted primes: Hausdorff dimension zero, Fourier decay, and absolute continuity
entries.abstract: We study the classical limiting laws of $\varphi(n)/n$ and $σ(n)/n$ over integers and shifted primes $p-1$. Let $μ_G$ denote the shifted-prime totient law and $μ_f$ its image under $x\mapsto-\log x$. The law $μ_G$ has Hausdorff dimension zero, while every Borel set of positive $μ_G$-measure has packing dimension one. All four ratio laws and their logarithmic images have lower and upper Shannon information dimensions satisfying $0.550<\underline{d}_1\le\overline{d}_1<0.571$. The law $μ_G$ gives full mass to absolutely normal Liouville numbers. Both $μ_G$ and $μ_f$ have quantitative Fourier decay. For $μ_f$, we obtain sharp concentration asymptotics and localize maximizing intervals. For $U_T$ uniform on $[0,T]$, $(\log T)\widehat{μ_f}(U_T)$ converges in distribution to a random Euler product with an independent uniform phase. For a uniform square matrix over $\mathbb{F}_p$, the probability of a primitive-root determinant tends, as the matrix size grows, to $c(p)=\frac{\varphi(p-1)}{p-1}\prod_{j\ge1}(1-p^{-j})$. Over primes, $c(p)$ has limiting law $μ_G$. In every fixed reduced progression, the empirical laws of $c(p)$ and $\varphi(p-1)/(p-1)$ over primes $p\le x$ converge to their common progression law with sharp Kolmogorov order $1/\log x$. We also obtain transport estimates in growing progressions. Strongly additive functions with prime values $(\log\ell)^{-A}$ have absolutely continuous integer and shifted-prime laws for every $A>0$, disproving the Erdős--Kátai singularity conjecture for $A>2$. Applications include extremal determinant bounds and certified prime selection without complete factorization of $p-1$. These results are unconditional; further quantitative refinements assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet $L$-functions.

entries.name: Proof of Rump's Retraction Conjecture for Quasilinear Cycle Sets
entries.abstract: Nondegenerate cycle sets were introduced by Rump as an algebraic framework for nondegenerate, involutive solutions to the Yang--Baxter equation. Nondegenerate cycle set structures on abelian groups, such as translation-invariant and quasilinear cycle sets, are of particular interest when studying the retraction problem in the theory of the Yang--Baxter equation. In this article, we solve the retraction problem for finite quasilinear cycle sets by showing that each nontrivial quasilinear cycle set is retractable, thus proving a conjecture of Rump.

entries.name: Local statistics and average rank of genus $g$ hyperelliptic curves with a Weierstrass point
entries.abstract: In this paper, we determine the probability that a genus $g$ hyperelliptic curve with a Weierstrass point over a number field has good reduction at a given prime of residue characteristic $>2g+1$. We also obtain analogous probability formulas for several other reduction types, including cases with positive toric or unipotent rank. As an application, assuming the Hasse--Weil conjecture and the generalized Riemann hypothesis, we derive an explicit upper bound for the average analytic rank of genus $g$ hyperelliptic curves with a Weierstrass point.

entries.name: Nahm Sums Dual to Zagier's Rank Three Examples and Related Identities
entries.abstract: In 2007, Zagier identified twelve families of candidates for rank three modular Nahm sums and established the modularity of three of them. The remaining cases were subsequently confirmed by Wang. Zagier's duality observation indicates that the Nahm sums associated with the duals of these examples might still be modular. We confirm that this is indeed true. The modularity of the dual of the sixth example was previously established by Milas and Wang, while that of the dual of the eleventh example was partially established by Shi and Wang. We settle all remaining cases, thereby establishing the modularity of every defined dual in Zagier's rank three list. We achieve this by proving new Rogers--Ramanujan type identities that express the relevant Nahm sums as finite sums of infinite products. Along the way we discover two new families of modular rank three Nahm sums. As applications, we prove some Nahm sum identities conjectured by Cao--Wang, Shi--Wang and Li.

entries.name: Characterization of $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule and lattice points in flagged hive polytopes
entries.abstract: We have previously, for a given positive integer $n$, explicitly characterized by certain linear inequalities the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux of shape length $2n$ or $2n-1$ produced by $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson (LR) rule. We now extend that characterization for lower shape lengths. Then using the composition of promotion operators defining the Naito-Suzuki-Watanabe bijection between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux and $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux, we also explicitly characterize by certain linear inequalities the corresponding $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux when the shape length is $2n$ or $2n-1$. In addition, when the given $n$ is $3$ or $ 4$ the $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight and the $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux via $1$-$0$-slack recording tableaux are characterized by linear inequalities for lower shape lengths. Since recording tableaux in the quantum Littlewood-Richardson rule are in natural bijection with Littlewood-Richardson-Sundaram (LRS) tableaux, we relate our results on the inverse quantum LR rule with other two bijections for the Naito-Sagaki conjecture and establish bijections between $\mathfrak{k}$-highest weight tableaux, $\widehat{\mathfrak{g}}$-dominant tableaux and the lattice points in a (disjoint) union of flagged hive polytopes.

entries.name: Martingale Transforms and Subsequence Estimates in Noncommutative \(L_p\)-Spaces
entries.abstract: We establish a transference principle from martingale transform inequalities to subsequence estimates for weakly null sequences. As applications, for every von Neumann algebra $\M$, (1) we show that, every bounded sequence in the Haagerup space $L_1(\M)=\M_*$ has either a norm-convergent subsequence or a $2$-co-lacunary subsequence, answering an open problem of Parcet and Randrianantoanina; (2) we prove that every UMD Banach space has the uniform USP, which in particular yields uniform USP for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<\infty$, answering a question posed by Oikhberg and Spinu; (3) we answer an open problem of Haagerup, Rosenthal and Sukochev for the upper $\ell_p$ estimates for $L_p(\M)$, $1<p<2$, in the affirmative; (4) we also answer the problem of whether every $2$-strictly singular operator on a noncommutative $L_1$-space is automatically Dunford--Pettis.

entries.name: Free boundary regularity for the porous medium equation
